title: Sell Mineral Rights in Trafford, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Trafford, AL | Jefferson County
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Trafford, AL, on the Jefferson-Blount county line? We check Black Warrior Basin coal seam gas activity nearby and offer a written cash price.
heroLead: Trafford straddles the Jefferson-Blount county line along Turkey Creek, a small town where a lot of mineral acreage has stayed in the same families since it was farmland.
intro: Trafford is small and rural even by northeast Jefferson County standards, and a good share of the land around it has never been platted for anything but farming or timber. That matters for mineral owners because tracts like these often carry clean, simple ownership: no subdivision, no multiple surface transfers, just a family farm with mineral rights that may or may not have ever seen a lease.

Because Trafford sits near the county line, we always double-check whether your legal description falls in Jefferson or Blount County before pricing anything, since the two counties have different production histories in the Black Warrior Basin.

sections.heading: Where Trafford falls in the Black Warrior fairway
paragraphs: The core of Black Warrior Basin coalbed methane production sits southwest of Trafford, closer to Oak Grove, Brookwood, and Cedar Cove. Trafford itself is on the northeastern edge of the historic coal seam trend, which generally means fewer producing wells directly nearby and more acreage that's held for its long-term optionality rather than current royalty income.

We still check current state permit and production data against your specific tract, because pockets of activity can sit closer to Trafford than the broad trend map suggests, especially where the Mary Lee and Pratt coal groups run shallower.

sections.heading: Farmland mineral reservations around Turkey Creek
paragraphs: A common pattern we see out of the Trafford area is a family that's farmed the same land for three or four generations, with the mineral rights never separately transferred, meaning whoever holds the surface today likely holds the minerals too. That's simpler to work with than a severed estate, but it still requires confirming the chain through probate if the land passed by inheritance rather than a recorded deed.

If your family's Trafford land was ever mortgaged, subdivided, or partially sold off, though, it's worth checking those records specifically, since even a single old transaction can carry a mineral reservation that changes what you actually own today.

sections.heading: Pricing a flank-acreage tract fairly
paragraphs: Because most Trafford-area minerals sit outside the current producing core, we price them primarily against comparable Jefferson County transfers and the trajectory of nearby CBM activity rather than an active royalty stream. That's a legitimate, if more modest, category of value, and we're upfront when a tract falls into it rather than inflating a number to make a sale.
If a lease or unit does exist on your acreage, even an old one, that changes the calculation meaningfully, so send us whatever paperwork you have and we'll factor it in before quoting.

faqs.question: Is my land actually in Jefferson County, or is it Blount?
faqs.answer: We check this first, since Trafford sits right on the line. Your deed's legal description will show the county, and if you're not sure, we can look it up from the parcel information you give us.

faqs.question: There's no lease on our family's land. Is it still worth anything?
faqs.answer: Often yes, though as speculative rather than producing acreage. We price that based on comparable transfers and nearby basin activity, and we'll tell you plainly which category your tract falls into.

faqs.question: We've farmed this land for generations and never split the minerals off. Does that make the sale simpler?
faqs.answer: Generally yes, since you likely hold both the surface and minerals together, which usually means a cleaner title check than a severed estate with multiple past owners.
